# Case study exercise: Neanderthal ancestry trajectory

In this case study exercise, you will be reproducing a critical result from [my
2018 study](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1814338116) on the limits of
selection against Neanderthal introgression, which turned into a study on the
importance of model assumptions on the robustness of inferences with $f_4$
statistics and $D$ statistics.

I chose this paper for several reasons:

1. This study would've been absolutely impossible to carry out without computer
simulations.

2. The limitations of tools I had available at the time required me to write
hundreds of lines of code spread across shell scripts, Python scripts, and R
scripts.

3. Thanks to _slendr_, a project which required months of work and lots of
coding is possible to reduce to a handful of lines of R.

4. It provides an excellent educational example of how _slendr_ simulations can
help you navigate any conceivable population genomic scenario, gain confidence
in your results, and aid in their interpretation.
